entries.note: The wizard runs against a checkout it does not own, so every install is skip-if-present and says so on stderr with the exact relative path the test asserts. This makes the action re-runnable on a partially integrated project: a second run fills only the gaps. Do not add a --force; a project that already owns editor.sh or a declaration is the authority on it.

The skeleton carries one inert format (match *.example, modes [raw], no command) instead of an empty array because contract 1 and contract 2 both require formats with minItems 1: an empty array would make readDeclaration settle the root as declared-with-error on the first open. Values are validated by regex before they reach printf, which is why the JSON can be emitted without a JSON writer; keep that validation if new fields are added. The game block is written only for contract 2 with both game arguments given.

entries.note: --dry-run must write nothing at all, so every effect goes through re_do, re_install or re_write_declaration and prints one '+ …' line on stdout while stage logs stay on stderr. The declaration prints '+ write .rengine/project.json' rather than a command because there is no command to name. Stage 1's read-only git checks still run under --dry-run: they are what makes the printed plan trustworthy.
